title: Power Rankings: Celtics sweep Texas, secure top spot
heading: 2007-08 Power Rankings: Week 21
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Hard to imagine how the Celts don't finish here three Mondays from now with their 23-5 record against the West and their 6-0 record on the road against the Lakers, Jazz, Rockets, Spurs, Mavericks and Pistons.

rankings.summaryHtml: Impossible to put the Hornets any lower when they're 8-3 in March and when they just followed up a rout of Houston by rallying from 15 down to stun the aforementioned team that just mowed through Texas.

rankings.summaryHtml: If they haven't impressed you yet with the league's longest active win streak, this might be the week for the Shaq-era Suns, depending on how they fare in this week's swing through Detroit, Boston and Philly.

rankings.summaryHtml: Nothing could have topped Boston's week, but the Lakers were at least in that zip code before losing at home to Golden State. Wins don't get much bigger than L.A.'s roadies in Dallas and Utah without Pau and Bynum.

rankings.summaryHtml: That loss to the short-handed Lakers didn't just put an end to Utah's 19-game winning streak at EnergySolutions Arena. It left us with no choice but to keep the Jazz, seemingly headed for a promotion, in their usual area.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Pistons don't lose two in a row very often, but road setbacks to the Cavs and Wizards have only made their chief rivals look better, preserving Boston's status as the league's only 50-win team for the third straight week.

rankings.summaryHtml: Would anyone be surprised if the Spurs, even after that 1-6 slide, win their division yet again? Be advised that the champs have only five more road games left, compared to seven for Houston and 10 for New Orleans.

rankings.summaryHtml: Golden State's next away victory clinches its first winning road record since 1993-94. But Sunday's W was its biggest roadie of the season, pushing the Warriors to just 2-16 all time against the Lakers at Staples Center.

rankings.summaryHtml: Good news: Portland should get the four Ws it needs to clinch a .500 season minus Greg Oden. Bad news: Portland inherits the NBA's longest playoff drought (five seasons) if Atlanta hangs on to No. 8 in the East.
